children: The S&P Global Germany Manufacturing PMI was revised slightly higher to 54.3 in August 2026 from a preliminary of 54.1, compared to 52.2 in July.

The reading showed that factory growth improved for a third straight month, reaching its strongest level since May 2022, driven by a solid rise in new orders, particularly in the intermediate goods sector, as well as stronger export sales.
There was a range of factors driving demand, including increased defence spending, data centre build-outs and stockpiling.
Also, the mood among businesses improved noticeably and is now the brightest seen since the Middle East conflict began.
However, there was also a worsening of supply chain pressures, which in turn contributed to a marked rise in purchasing activity as firms looked to secure supplies of inputs.
Average prices paid for purchases meanwhile rose at the slowest rate since the start of the Middle East conflict, but one that was still elevated by historical standards.

title: Germany Manufacturing PMI Revised Up
